audit.title: Migrating from VRF v2
audit.summary: This is a well-structured, terminology-consistent VRF v2→v2.5 migration guide with strong primary-source linking (GitHub contract sources, Remix samples) and a crisp dated opening claim. Its single biggest GEO strength is clean sectioning with no heading skips; its single biggest weakness is machine-readability — the deterministic scanner found **zero fenced code blocks, zero JSON-LD, no canonical URL, and no last-updated date**, meaning agents parsing the served HTML likely cannot extract the Solidity examples that are the page's core value. A comparison table and symptom-phrased headings are the highest-leverage additions. Honest verdict: solid content undercut by parseability and metadata gaps that suppress its retrievability and agent-usability.

recommendations.title: Add a v2 → v2.5 change-comparison table
recommendations.where: top of "Code changes", before the tab components
recommendations.issue: "0 table(s)"; changes are narrated across prose + nested tabs
recommendations.change: Insert a table with rows for each breaking change — Consumer base (`VRFConsumerBaseV2`→`VRFConsumerBaseV2Plus`), Coordinator (`VRFCoordinatorV2Interface`→`VRFCoordinatorV2_5`), subscription ID type (`uint64`→`uint256`), request format (positional args→`VRFV2PlusClient.RandomWordsRequest`), and the new `extraArgs`/`nativePayment` field — columns V2 | V2.5.
recommendations.why: tables are extracted verbatim as justified answers; this is the single most reusable liftable unit for "what changed in VRF v2.5."

recommendations.title: Ensure code blocks are parseable fenced blocks
recommendations.issue: scanner reports "0 fenced block(s)… languages: [none]" despite visible Solidity
recommendations.change: verify the rendered HTML emits standard `<pre><code class="language-solidity">` (or de-nest fences from JSX indentation) so parsers detect them; confirm each block carries a language class.
recommendations.why: if agents can't detect the code, the page's core value is invisible to the tools most likely to use it during a migration task.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/error-phrased troubleshooting headings
recommendations.issue: no error-string or "why won't it compile" coverage
recommendations.change: add H3s phrased as queries, e.g. "Type mismatch: subscription ID is `uint256` in v2.5", "`fulfillRandomWords` signature mismatch (memory vs calldata)", "Wrapper constructor no longer takes the LINK token address" — each with the one-line fix.
recommendations.why: devs/agents query by symptom; the page already contains these facts in body prose but not as retrievable question-shaped headings.

recommendations.title: Add TechArticle JSON-LD, canonical, and last-updated
recommendations.change: emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with `headline`, `dateModified`, `about: "Chainlink VRF v2.5"`, and a self-referential `canonical` link; surface a visible "Last updated" line.
recommendations.why: freshness and canonical signals raise trust and dedupe; migration docs are especially penalized when undated.

recommendations.title: Make the subscription-ID type change answer-first and quotable
recommendations.issue: one-line note; easy to skim past
recommendations.change: lead with a standalone claim: "In VRF v2.5 the subscription ID is `uint256`, not the `uint64` used in v2 — update every declaration, constructor parameter, and mapping key." Add an explicit Don't: "Don't keep `uint64 s_subscriptionId` — it will not compile against `VRFConsumerBaseV2Plus`."
recommendations.why: models default to the familiar v2 `uint64` prior; naming the wrong pattern as a Don't defends against it.

recommendations.title: Replace deferred billing vagueness with concrete numbers
recommendations.issue: "The amount of wrapper overhead gas is reduced compared to V2" (no figure)
recommendations.change: state the actual percentage-premium mechanism and a representative overhead-gas value/example inline, even if full tables stay on the Billing page.
recommendations.why: quantitative claims are among the highest-lift edits; "reduced" is not liftable.

recommendations.title: Define new APIs at first use
recommendations.issue: "Add the `setCoordinator` function… so that you can easily update the VRF coordinator"
recommendations.change: add a one-sentence definition: "`setCoordinator(address)` lets contract owners point the consumer at a new VRF coordinator without redeploying." Similarly define `extraArgs`/`ExtraArgsV1`.
recommendations.why: crisp definitions near first use are preferentially quoted.

antiPatterns: Vague quantifier "many" and unquantified "reduced… overhead gas" in Billing — replace with figures.
`...` elisions inside otherwise-complete Solidity examples reduce copy-paste runnability (mitigated by Remix links).
No dated/last-updated signal on a time-sensitive migration page.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced at the top — good; confirm this page is enumerated in it.
Site-level JSON-LD/canonical templating likely governs the metadata gaps; fix at the layout level rather than per-page.
The CLI did not capture `<head>`; pass raw head HTML next run to confirm the schema/canonical findings beyond the served-HTML scan.
